hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? what sound tells you it’s time for something? an alarm, a bell, a voice?
options: same for most people. today, a call that isn’t an alarm.
nice. today’s call is a human voice too.
that’s okay. today, a sound worth stopping for.

steps.line: When the Muslims first came to Medina, there was no call to prayer. People gathered by guessing the time.
So they talked it over. Ring a bell? Blow a horn? Light a fire?

steps.q: That night, a companion named ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd had a dream. What do you think it gave him?
o: The sound of a new bell
steps.why: Words, taught to him by a stranger in the dream. The report is in Abu Dawud: not a new sound, but words anyone could learn.

steps.line: ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd dreamed of a man carrying a bell. Instead of selling it, the man taught him words: Allahu akbar, God is greatest.
In the morning he told the Prophet ﷺ. “It is a true dream,” he said. “Teach it to Bilal. His voice carries further.”
So Bilal called. The man once held under a rock for saying “one” now called a whole city to the One.

steps.q: Why might a voice have been better than a bell or a horn?
o: Bells were too costly to make
A voice can say what you’re called to
steps.why: A bell only says now. A voice says what for: God is greatest, come to prayer, come to success.

steps.q: When Bilal first called, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab hurried to the Prophet ﷺ. Why?
o: To ask who had chosen Bilal
He had dreamed the very same words
To say the call was too loud
steps.why: Reports in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi say ‘Umar heard the call and said he had seen the same dream. Two dreamers, one call.

steps.line: Today, five times a day, the same words rise from city rooftops, one voice a beat behind another, never quite in sync.
steps.label: today

steps.q: You hear the adhan from a phone in the kitchen. A saying of the Prophet ﷺ suggests something to do. What?
o: Stop and face Mecca right away
Repeat the words softly after the caller
steps.why: Repeat each line after the caller, says a hadith in Muslim. At “come to prayer” many say instead, “there is no power or strength except with God.”

steps.line: And whoever hears the call, a saying teaches, repeats it softly, line by line. Even in a kitchen, from a phone, mid-cup of tea.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. they could have chosen a bell. instead the call became a human voice, saying exactly what it calls you to.
in islam, the adhan is called at each of the five prayer times. and a saying teaches that everything that hears it, near or far, will bear witness for the one who calls.

steps.q: A bell says “now.” The adhan says “come to prayer, come to success.” What does that suggest prayer is, in Islam?
o: An interruption to get through quickly
A success you are invited to, not just a time
A duty only for those who can hear it
steps.why: Hayya ‘ala l-falah: come to success. The call treats prayer as the win of the day, not a break from it.

today.say: today, listen to one adhan, from a nearby mosque, a recording, or a prayer app. it’s your choice: just listen, learn the first line, or repeat it softly after the caller, as many muslims do.
options: lovely. that’s what the word means: the thing you hear.

sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 604; Sahih Muslim 377 (Ibn ‘Umar: in Medina they gathered and estimated the time of prayer, with no one calling; some said use a bell like the Christians’, others a horn like the Jews’; ‘Umar suggested a man to call; “O Bilal, get up and call to prayer”)
Sahih al-Bukhari 603 (Anas: they mentioned fire and the bell)

Sunan Abi Dawud 499; Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 189 (‘Abdullah ibn Zayd’s dream of a man carrying a bell who taught him the words; “It is a true vision”; “teach it to Bilal, for his voice is more far-reaching than yours”; graded hasan sahih)
Sahih al-Bukhari 609 (no jinn, human or anything else hears the caller’s voice but will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection)
Sahih al-Bukhari 611; Sahih Muslim 383 (when you hear the call, say what the caller says)
